title: PPA-Aware Power Grid Optimization Techniques for Congested High Frequency Datapath Designs
problem: High-frequency networking switch designs require robust power grid optimization to handle congested signal routing while meeting stringent power, performance, and area (PPA) constraints, particularly regarding voltage drop and electromigration reliability.
motivation: Dense packing of datapath logic in high-frequency designs creates severe power grid challenges. Traditional layout approaches struggle to balance signal congestion, voltage drop, and reliability under PPA constraints.
method: Semi-custom layout approach with clustering and placement-aware optimization of datapath structures. Treats critical datapaths as logical units for coordinated power grid and signal routing optimization.
key_novelty: Clustering-based grouping of datapath cells with coordinated placement enabling efficient layout quality improvements while meeting voltage drop and reliability verification constraints.
contributions: 17% improvement in voltage drop (IR) for custom designs
Method for achieving PPA tradeoff analysis in congested high-frequency designs
Integration with EMIR (Electromigration and IR) analysis tools
limitations: Abstract describes methodology conceptually; no specific area, power consumption, or frequency numbers provided. Limited to single design case study.
primary_theme: Power grid optimization for high-frequency datapaths
